title: Business Administrator
description:
We are recruiting a Business Administrator for a client in Leeds. This is a varied and hands-on role that will sit at the heart of the day-to-day operation of the business. The successful candidate will provide support across procurement, supplier management, finance, project administration, logistics and general business operations.

The position would suit somebody who enjoys working in a broad role where no two days are quite the same and who is comfortable coordinating activity across suppliers, projects, finance and internal teams.

Business Administrator - The Role

Working closely with engineering, project and management teams, you will help ensure that purchasing, administration and operational processes run efficiently and accurately.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Managing day-to-day purchasing activities and raising purchase orders.
- Monitoring supplier deliveries, lead times and outstanding orders. Maintaining supplier records and supporting supplier onboarding.
- Liaising with suppliers and expediting orders where required. Supporting supplier performance monitoring and administration.
- Assisting with project procurement planning and tracking project expenditure and purchase commitments.
- Supporting project reporting, schedules and action trackers.
- Assisting with accounts payable, accounts receivable, cashflow forecasting and expenditure tracking.
- Supporting monthly management reporting, budgeting and financial planning activities.
- Providing administrative support for payroll, VAT and other business reporting requirements. Maintaining accurate information within the company's ERP/business management system.
- Processing goods receipts, purchasing transactions and inventory movements. Coordinating incoming and outgoing shipments.
- Preparing shipping and export documentation where required. Supporting stock control, stock takes and inventory accuracy.
- Coordinating the movement of materials between suppliers, customers and company facilities.
- Organising travel, accommodation, meetings and occasional company events.
- Maintaining company records, documentation and filing systems.
- Supporting quality, health & safety and compliance administration.
- Identifying opportunities to improve administrative and operational processes.

Business Administrator - About You

We are looking for an experienced administrator who is comfortable working across several areas of a business and managing multiple priorities.

You are likely to have:
- At least 5 years' experience within business administration, procurement administration, finance administration, project support or a similarly broad operational role.
- Previous experience working within an engineering, manufacturing or technology environment.
- A good understanding of purchasing and supplier management processes.
- Strong organisational and coordination skills.
- Strong Microsoft Office and general IT skills.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- The ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively with limited supervision.

Business Administrator - The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to take on a genuinely varied position within an engineering-led organisation, with responsibility spanning procurement, finance, projects, logistics and wider business administration.

The role will suit somebody who enjoys creating structure, keeping operations organised and becoming a trusted point of contact for colleagues, suppliers and other stakeholders.

If you are an experienced Business Administrator looking for a broad role within an engineering or manufacturing environment, we would be interested in hearing from you. Please do apply now!

title: Care Navigator/ Medical Receptionist
description: South Queen Street Medical Centre are looking to appoint a care navigator/ receptionist to join our busy GP practice who will be the first point of contact for patients, contractors, and visitors as well as carrying out general office management tasks. Working pattern 5 hours per day, 5 days a week, alternate weekly am & pm shifts, 8am-630pm. Flexibility and overtime will be required for this role. You will be responsible for the general reception duties within the Practice and work with our established processes, policies, and procedures to provide a comprehensive high-quality service and deal efficiently and courteously with patient enquiries. You will receive, assist, and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. You will provide general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. You will have excellent communication skills, a compassionate and friendly nature who can operate in a busy environment with a range of people and professions, as you will be working with our clinical and administration teams. Welcome patients in a friendly, respectful and professional manner. Respond to general enquiries and provide accurate information about practice services, opening hours and appointment procedures. Deal sensitively with patients who may be anxious, distressed, frustrated or experiencing difficult personal circumstances. Maintain a clean, organised and welcoming reception and waiting area. Manage challenging situations professionally and escalate complaints or concerns to the appropriate member of the practice team. Care Navigation and Appointment Management Handle patient requests for appointments, advice and access to healthcare services by telephone and in person. Use approved care navigation protocols to direct patients to the most appropriate clinician or service, including GPs, practice nurses, clinical pharmacists, physiotherapists and other available services where appropriate. Gather relevant non-clinical information to help determine the appropriate appointment pathway, without attempting to diagnose medical conditions. Book, amend and cancel appointments using the practices clinical computer system. Identify potentially urgent concerns in accordance with practice procedures and promptly escalate them to a clinician. Provide information about alternative services, such as NHS 111, where appropriate and in accordance with practice guidance. Maintain accurate records of patient contacts and appointment requests. Telephone and Administrative Duties Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and manage a busy call queue efficiently. Handle patient messages and ensure they are passed to the appropriate member of the clinical or administrative team. Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice policies and direct medication queries to the appropriate professional. Register new patients and update demographic details, contact information and other relevant records. Manage incoming and outgoing post, emails and electronic communications. Assist with administrative tasks, including recalling patients for appointments, supporting clinical audits and maintaining accurate practice records. Monitor outstanding administrative tasks and follow up requests within agreed timescales. Clinical Systems and Data Management Use the practices electronic clinical system, SystmOne, to access and update patient information. Ensure patient details, appointment information and messages are recorded accurately and promptly. Handle sensitive patient information securely and maintain strict confidentiality at all times. Comply with UK GDPR, data protection legislation, information governance requirements and practice policies. Follow procedures for accessing, storing and sharing patient information appropriately. Teamwork and Practice Support Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants, pharmacists, care coordinators and administrative colleagues. Attend staff meetings and training sessions as required. Support colleagues during busy periods and assist with the day-to-day organisation of reception services. Follow practice policies relating to health and safety, infection prevention, safeguarding and equality and diversity. Report incidents, risks and concerns to the appropriate manager. Undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role to support the effective operation of the practice. Training and Development The successful candidate will receive induction and training appropriate to the role, including practice procedures, clinical systems, information governance, confidentiality, safeguarding, health and safety and care navigation. Ongoing training and development will be encouraged to support the delivery of a safe, efficient and high-quality patient service. Personal Qualities We are looking for someone who is approachable, empathetic, dependable and proactive. The successful candidate must demonstrate patience, discretion and professionalism when dealing with sensitive situations and be committed to treating every patient with dignity, respect and fairness. Working hours, salary, annual leave and other employment terms will be confirmed during recruitment.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Abbey Grange Medical Practice is looking for a part time receptionist to join our friendly experienced team on a fixed term 12 month contract with a view to the position continuing after the fixed term period. The successful applicant will be working 24 hours per week over 4 days. Primary frontline contact for patients, managing patient access, communications, and administrative workflows within the practice including: Greeting and Check-in Telephone Management Care Navigation Prescription Processing Data Entry & Records Correspondence & Post New Patient Registrations Job Summary: - To assist patients both face-to-face and on the telephone with booking appointments, requests for information or access to other services provided by the practice. - To work as an effective member of the reception team ensuring that all day-to-day delegated tasks are administered to agreed timescales. - To maintain an effective patient recall system for chronic disease management. - To provide general admin duties as required Main Duties and Responsibilities: Reception - To greet patients and direct them as appropriate, maintaining a high level of professionalism at all times. - Ensure patients are checked in when arriving for appointments on the appointment system. - Signpost patients to the correct clinician or service - Accepting requests for and handing out repeat prescriptions. - Handing out letters, completed forms etc., accepting the appropriate fee and issuing a receipt. - Registration of new patients and temporary residents. - Explaining about surgery procedures. - Keeping the waiting room clean and tidy. Telephone - Receive incoming calls and deal with queries appropriately and professionally. - Record all messages in the appropriate manner according to the practice policy & workflow. - Take details of visits in accordance with practice procedure. - Order ambulances when required. - Contact & liaise with patients delivering information and messages as instructed by the GP including informing patients of test results. Computer - To book appointments or amend when required - Raise and issue repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice procedures - Scan hospital letters and other correspondence into the clinical system ensuring that they are attached to the correct patient record. - To use the choose & book system for patient choice referrals - Maintain a recall system in accordance with practice procedure for calling in patients for routine review. - General administrative duties as requested by the practice manager or admin manager Confidentiality : In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety : The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines. Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills. Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards. Reporting potential risks

title: GP Receptionist
description: Idle Medical Centre is seeking an enthusiastic Receptionist to join our team. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of an innovative team focused on delivering patient-centred care in a collaborative and supportive environment. Were a friendly, forward-thinking practice over-looking the village of Idle. We have a traditional approach to general practice, striving to offer the best service to our patients wherever possible. We strongly believe in supporting and investing in the practice team. Our ethos has always been to bring in the right people and build something better. If you think that might be you, then wed love to hear from you. This role offers the opportunity to become a part of a thriving team within a positive work environment. The successful applicant will join our dedicated and friendly Reception Team who are often the first contact our patients have with the practice. You will be part of a busy, thriving GP practice, where our reception team is central to ensuring a smooth and supportive experience for our patients. The role will involve answering the phones, manning the reception desk, booking appointments, assisting patients with queries and managing general administration tasks that support our day-to-day patient care. All general duties and responsibilities associated with a GP Receptionist: Answer the phones and book appointments, sometimes during very busy periods, while managing patient expectations. Staff the reception desk, booking patients in and dealing with enquiries. General administrative tasks to support patient care. The use of SystmOne to manage patient records. Utilise and demonstrate sensitive communication styles, to ensure patients are fully informed and understanding. Recognise the need for alternative methods of communication to overcome different levels of understanding, cultural background and preferred ways of communicating. Prioritise, organise and manage own workload in a manner that maintains and promotes quality. Work as an effective and responsible team member to support each other and continually improve the service. Support the equality and diversity of patients, carers and colleagues by recognising the importance of peoples rights and interpreting them in a way that is consistent with policy, procedures and current legislation. Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues by behaving in a manner which is welcoming, non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Work with your line manager to undertake continual personal and professional development, access regular supervision and take an active part in reviewing and developing the roles and responsibilities of the post. Undertake any tasks consistent with the level of the post and the scope of the role, ensuring that work is delivered in a timely and effective manner. Duties may vary from time to time, without changing the general character of the post or the level of responsibility.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Kensington Partnership is seeking a friendly, professional and organised Medical Receptionist to join our busy GP practice team. The successful candidate will provide efficient reception and administrative support, ensuring patients receive a welcoming and professional service. Excellent communication, IT and organisational skills are essential, along with the ability to work under pressure, use initiative and work effectively as part of a team. Previous NHS, GP reception or SystmOne experience is desirable, but full training will be provided. Flexibility to cover staff absences and work across practice sites where required is also desirable. Recruitment Process Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a pre-interview information session on Thursday, 19 November 2026, from 1:00 pm to 3:00 pm , to gain a better understanding of the role and its expectations. Those who remain interested will be invited to a formal interview at a later date. You will join a supportive, forward-thinking team, delivering professional and compassionate patient services within a busy primary care environment. With most incoming calls managed through our AI system, the role primarily involves handling face-to-face enquiries, supporting AI-assisted triage and providing administrative support. Responsibilities include reviewing and processing patient requests, maintaining accurate records, directing enquiries to appropriate teams and escalating clinical concerns in accordance with practice procedures. Occasional telephone duties may also be required. A courteous, confidential and patient-centred approach is essential at all times. Reception and Patient Services Welcome patients and manage face-to-face enquiries professionally and courteously. Handle calls transferred by the AI telephone system requiring receptionist assistance. Support AI-assisted triage by reviewing and processing patient requests in line with practice procedures. Book appointments following triage outcomes and provide appropriate care navigation. Signpost patients to relevant services and escalate urgent or complex concerns to the clinical team. Administration and Practice Support Maintain accurate patient records using SystmOne and other practice systems. Process correspondence, home visit requests, ambulance transport and interpreter bookings. Handle payments, receipts, deliveries and general administrative duties. Provide day-to-day administrative support to GPs, clinical staff and colleagues. Communication and Teamwork Communicate professionally and compassionately with patients, carers, colleagues and external agencies. Work collaboratively and flexibly across practice sites as required. Support patients with additional communication or accessibility needs. Undertake chaperone duties when appropriately trained and authorised. Confidentiality and Information Governance Maintain strict confidentiality and access patient records only when authorised and necessary. Comply with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and practice information governance policies. Promptly report suspected data breaches, security incidents or confidentiality concerns. General Responsibilities Assist with opening and securing practice premises when authorised. Maintain a safe, tidy and welcoming reception environment. Follow safeguarding, infection prevention, health and safety, and other practice policies. Complete mandatory training and undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role.

title: GP Receptionist

At Crofton & Sharlston Medical Practice, we are proud to provide high-quality, patient-centred healthcare to almost 11,000 patients across our two practice sites. We are committed to delivering safe, effective, and compassionate care while continually developing and improving the services we offer to our local community. Location: Primarily based at Crofton Health Centre, with occasional work at our branch site in Sharlston when required. Hours: Part-time 32 hours per week Working Monday to Friday between 8:00am and 6:30pm proposed hours: Monday 8.00am 6.30pm (30 mins unpaid lunch break), Tuesday 12.30-6.30pm, Wed & Thurs 12.30-5.30pm, Friday 12.30-6.30pm Reports to:Administration Manager and Senior Receptionist What We Are Looking For We are seeking a polite, professional, friendly, and highly motivated individual who can: Work well independently and as part of a team Stay calm and professional when dealing with patients in all situations Follow practice policies and procedures accurately Maintain confidentiality and professionalism at all times Key Skills & Requirements Excellent telephone manner and communication skills Strong IT skills Good organisational and time management skills Good standard of education Relevant administrative qualifications (desirable) Previous experience is desirable but not essential we value the right attitude and commitment to learning. If youre looking to be part of a supportive and dynamic team in a well-established healthcare setting, wed love to hear from you! Reception Answer all calls promptly and care navigate to the correct service in accordance with practice protocol. Receive patients consulting with members of Practice team, directing to appropriate health care professional. Process appointment requests for appointments from patients by telephone and in person. Deal with visit requests Process repeats prescription requests in accordance with Practice guidelines. Promote services to patients. Deal with and complete queries/enquiries as per the practices protocols. Sort post Replenish stationary. Other Tasks At the end of the day, check surgeries, replenish stock, and make sure all areas are clean, tidy, and ready for the next day as per practice protocols. Ensure building security is maintained in accordance with CQC guidelines. Any other tasks allocated by Senior Administrators/Practice Manager Confidentiality: While seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, Practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the Practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the Practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the Practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the Practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to Practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks. Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills. Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified Equality and Diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers, and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with Practice procedures and policies, and current legislation. Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers, and colleagues. Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the Practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Attend and actively participate in all staff training and regular reception meetings. Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development. Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the Practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs. Effectively manage own time, workload, and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members. Communicate effectively with patients and carers. Communicate effectively with Secondary care and other associated health care agencies Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply Practice policies, standards, and guidance. Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work. Participate in audit where appropriate.

title: GP Receptionist / Care Navigator
description: We are recruiting for a Care Navigator to join our team. The role will be part time, and you must be available to work Friday evenings up until 18:30pm. Working within the Robin Lane reception team, the post-holder will help provide a friendly and welcoming service for all patients. The Care Navigator will support patients to access the right health care in a professional and efficient manner. Follow practice processes to actively signpost patients to the most appropriate healthcare professional and service, whilst handling any complex queries and challenging situations in a professional manner, ensuring any issues are resolved where possible, at the first point of contact. Assist both clinical and admin colleagues with the smooth running of the reception area and surgery building.The post-holder is expected to comply with the employment policies and procedures, with due regard to clinical and information governance policies and procedures, and any other policies and procedures necessary for the safe and effective discharge of the duties contained within this document. This job description is subject to a flexibility clause and may change according to business requirements. This advert may close early should the right candidate be found. To welcome patients presenting either in person or by telephone; ensuring you respond promptly and positively. Book appointments for patients and cancel appointments where needed. Support patients in navigating to the most appropriate service, which may include informing patients of external health care providers and online services. Effectively handle all queries that present at the practice; problem solving, signposting and escalation of matters, as appropriate. Ensure patient records are accurate and kept up to date and that all patient contacts are documented in the system using the Care Navigation Template. Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team members and associated healthcare providers. Carrying out administrative duties which include scanning, tasks, out of hours reports, new patient registrations (including basic urine dip), opening and sorting of post (both internal and external), photocopying reports, updating patient details, filing INR reports and data inputting as requested. Processing medication requests, including issuing repeat medication and appliance items, as well as forwarding patient requests onto the practice pharmacy team/on-call GP. Communicating effectively with local pharmacy staff and resolving/investigating any queries they may have. Processing e-consults via system one and triaging the patient accordingly using signposting where necessary. Opening up/locking up of practice premises and maintaining security in accordance with practice protocols. Carry out chronic disease recalls and vaccination campaigns, booking relevant appointments working from a list to ensure clinics are fully utilised Informing patients of test results and following up with instructions from clinicians. Keeping the reception area and notice boards clean, tidy and up to date. Taking payments for private documents from patients and providing receipts Support all clinical staff with general tasks as required. Assisting the Site Co-ordinator with weekly fire alarm checks and weekly/monthly legionella testing, when required. Assisting the Site Co-ordinator with weekly room plans and petty cash records, when required. To be able to work with people from a wide variety of cultures and backgrounds, and people with disabilities and learning difficulties, and to be able to communicate with them (and, when necessary, their carers) appropriately to facilitate their care and understanding of their care within the service. Attend and positively contribute to team meetings. Fully comply with all company Health and Safety requirements, including reporting all accidents, near accidents, and hazards. Treat all patients fairly and with respect. Provide cover across all sites as required. This is not an exhaustive list, and it is expected that this role will develop as the business grows.

title: Clinical Administrator
description: An exciting opportunity has arisen for an enthusiastic, self-motivated and flexible individual to join our established Living Well 18-Week Admin Hub , based in the Huddersfield area. You will play a vital role in supporting clinicians within a busy service, helping ensure patients receive a professional, responsive and positive experience throughout their care journey. We're looking for someone who: Puts people first providing caring, professional and compassionate customer service to patients, colleagues and visitors. Thrives in a busy environment staying organised, prioritising tasks and supporting the smooth running of the service. Takes a proactive approach using initiative, embracing a can-do attitude and finding practical solutions. Works as part of a team communicating effectively and working flexibly to meet the needs of the service. You will join a well-established team where you will be supported in your role and have the opportunity to contribute to a service that makes a real difference to local people. title: Care Navigator/Receptionist
description: Due to a member of the team upskilling into a new role, we are seeking a Care Navigator/Receptionist to join our fast-paced reception and administration team. We are looking for individuals who feel they will be able to settle into a busy practice, whilst able to work independently and as part of a team. Previous primary care or GP surgery experience is desirable, although applicants with relevant transferable skills will also be considered. Provide a professional and welcoming first point of contact for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals. Manage a busy telephone system, responding to enquiries and directing patients to the most appropriate service. Book, amend and cancel patient appointments in accordance with practice protocols. Receive patients at the reception desk, recording arrivals and assisting with enquiries. Process repeat prescription requests in line with practice procedures. Deal with incoming emails, post and other administrative correspondence. Liaise effectively with GPs, nurses, pharmacists, hospitals and other healthcare organisations. Carry out administrative tasks relating to patient records, including scanning, document management and filing. Follow practice protocols to ensure consistent and high-quality care is provided to our patients. Act as directed by other members of the practice team. Provide reception and administrative cover for colleagues during periods of annual leave or sickness absence. Work across both Ireland Wood and Horsforth practice sites when required. Ensure confidentiality is always maintained in accordance with General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and practice policies. The Care Navigator/Receptionist is an essential member of the practice team, providing a professional, efficient and patient-focused reception and administrative service across both practice sites. Working closely with the Practice Manager, GP Partners and the wider clinical and administrative teams, the post-holder will help ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the practice while delivering excellent customer service to patients and visitors. A key part of the role is supporting patients with their queries and appointment requests, helping them to access the most appropriate healthcare professional or service in line with practice protocols. The post-holder will manage appointments, respond to telephone and face-to-face enquiries, process repeat prescription requests and undertake a range of administrative duties to support the delivery of safe and effective patient care. The role also includes maintaining accurate patient records, processing correspondence and supporting communication with hospitals, pharmacies and other healthcare organisations. The post-holder will work in accordance with practice policies, maintain confidentiality at all times, and provide cover for colleagues and across both practice sites when required. Overall, this is a varied and rewarding role that requires excellent communication, organisational and IT skills, together with the ability to work calmly and effectively in a busy environment while providing a high standard of patient care and customer service.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Stanley Health Centre is looking for an enthusiastic, flexible and reliable receptionist to join our Reception team. Successful candidates will need to be able to demonstrate previous administrative and customer service experience and have the skills to adapt to and prioritise the duties of a busy reception desk, remaining calm and focused to ensure a high standard of care is delivered to patients. The ideal candidate will be a team player with excellent verbal and written communication skills. Computer skills are essential, and experience with a clinical system would be advantageous, but training will be provided for the right candidate. The post holder will also need to be flexible in their hours to cover either mornings or afternoons when required, working part-time 25 hours per week either 8am to 1pm or 1.30pm 6.30pm Monday to Friday. Stanley Health Centre Receptionist job description Job Title: Medical Receptionist Line Manager: Assistant Practice Manager Accountable to: Practice Manager Hours per week: 25 To be responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and the provision of general support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties can include but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, processing of information and assisting patients as required. To act as the central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with multidisciplinary team members and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. Mission Statement We will strive to: Provide a service which puts patients needs and welfare at the heart of everything we do. Generic Responsibilities All staff at Stanley Health Centre have a duty to conform to the following: Equality, Diversity & Inclusion A good attitude and positive action towards ED&I creates and environment where all individuals are able to achieve their full potential. Creating such an environment is important for three reasons: it improves operational effectiveness, it is morally the right thing to do, and it is required by law. Patients and their families have the right to be treated fairly and be routinely involved in decisions about their treatment and care. They can expect to be treated with dignity and respect and will not be discriminated against on any grounds including age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. Patients have a responsibility to treat other patients and our staff with dignity and respect. Staff have the right to be treated fairly in recruitment and career progression. Staff can expect to work in an environment where diversity is valued and equality of opportunity is promoted. Staff will not be discriminated against on any grounds including age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. Staff have a responsibility to ensure that you treat our patients and their colleagues with dignity and respect. Safety, Health, Environment and Fire (SHEF) This practice is committed to supporting and promoting opportunities to for staff to maintain their health, well-being and safety. You have a duty to take reasonable care of health and safety at work for you, your team and others, and to cooperate with employers to ensure compliance with health and safety requirements. All personnel are to comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, Environmental Protection Act 1990, Environment Act 1995, Fire Precautions (workplace) Regulations 1999 and other statutory legislation. Confidentiality This practice is committed to maintaining an outstanding confidential service. Patients entrust and permit us to collect and retain sensitive information relating to their health and other matters, pertaining to their care. They do so in confidence and have a right to expect all staff will respect their privacy and maintain confidentiality at all times. It is essential that if, the legal requirements are to be met and the trust of our patients is to be retained that all staff protect patient information and provide a confidential service. Quality & Continuous Improvement (CI) To preserve and improve the quality of our output, all personnel are required to think not only of what they do, but how they achieve it. By continually re-examining our processes, we will be able to develop and improve the overall effectiveness of the way we work. The responsibility for this rests with everyone working within the practice to look for opportunities to improve quality and share good practice. This practice continually strives to improve work processes which deliver health care with improved results across all areas of our service provision. We promote a culture of continuous improvement, where everyone counts and staff are permitted to make suggestions and contributions to improve our service delivery and enhance patient care. Induction Training On arrival at the practice all personnel are to complete a practice induction programme; this is managed by the Deputy Practice Manager. Learning and Development The effective use of training and development is fundamental in ensuring that all staff are equipped with the appropriate skills, knowledge, attitude and competences to perform their role. All staff will be required to partake and complete mandatory training as directed by the training coordinator, as well as participating in the practice training programme. Staff will also be permitted (subject to approval) to undertake external training courses which will enhance their knowledge and skills, progress their career and ultimately, enable them to improve processes and service delivery. Collaborative Working All staff are to recognise the significance of collaborative working. Teamwork is essential in multidisciplinary environments. Effective communication is essential and all staff must ensure they communicate in a manner which enables the sharing of information in an appropriate manner. Service Delivery Staff at Stanley Health Centre must adhere to the information contained with practice policies and regional directives, ensuring protocols are adhered to at all times. Staff will be given detailed information during the induction process regarding policy and procedure. Security The security of the practice is the responsibility of all personnel. Staff must ensure they remain vigilant at all times and report any suspicious activity immediately to their line manager. Under no circumstances are staff to share the codes for the door locks to anyone and are to ensure that restricted areas remain effectively secured. Professional Conduct Practice staff are required to dress appropriately for their role. Administrative staff will be provided with a uniform whilst clinical staff must dress in accordance with their role. Leave All personnel are entitled to take leave. Line managers are to ensure all of their staff are afforded the opportunity to take their allocated amount of annual leave each year, and should be encouraged to take all of their leave entitlement.

title: MEDICAL RECEPTIONIST
description: We need a reliable, motivated, hard working and flexible individual to join our friendly busy team. Must have SystmOne experience withgood computer and communication skills. To work 25.5 hours per week To commence as soon as possible. FLEXIBILITY IS ESSENTIAL TO THIS ROLE. Greeting and directing patients and visitors on arrival. Signposting patients to the most appropriate healthcare professional. Registering new patients. Booking appointments. Using photocopier, telephone, email and clinical system. Respond to the needs of clinicians during surgery. Respond to requests from Management. Preparing consultation rooms, prior to and after surgery. General housekeeping (e.g. keeping waiting and office areas clean and tidy). Action tasks on SystmOne Provide clerical assistance to support the delivery of patient services, e.g. post, data input and scanning. Specified Duties To provide and effective, polite and efficient point of contact to all patients and visitors to the Practice. To create and instil an atmosphere of calm, pleasant and peaceful surrounds. Maintain a positive attitude at all times. Smile when you answer the phone. Remember never say it is not my job to. Always say what you can do, not what you cannot do. Acknowledge and welcome the arrival of patients with a booked appointment at the front desk. Make future appointments and allocate appropriate same day appointments. Liaise with duty doctor via SystmOne any instructions regarding the processing of lists that are undertaken in line with the agreed procedure. Answer the telephone within 4 rings and ensure all messages are recorded in SystmOne and are dealt with or passed to the appropriate person for action. Deal with actions arising from the post when dealt with by the duty doctor. Deal with prescriptions requests and home visit requests as they come in, on the telephone and face to face. Make up a visit list each day and print out a patient summary relating to each person being visited. Exhibit willingness to train on new technology and updated systems, as required. Ensure all aspects of Health and safety are adhered to and breaches reported to Management. Flexibility when asked to cover shifts for holidays, sickness, absences remember you never know when you might need cover. Generally keeping the reception area, in fact all areas clean and tidy. Scan all post into SystmOne record as agreed. Ensure accurate data entry onto SystmOne according to protocols. Liaise with other Health Care professionals, as and when necessary to ensure relevant people are advised of developments, which affect patients under their care. To work in a manner that ensures the smooth running of the Practice. Receiving and receipting monies. Using email facilities as an internal communication tool. At the end of the day ensure all areas of reception are tidy in order to ensure easy accessibility for the cleaners. To ensure all areas are secure at night, all electrical equipment is switched off and that the building is secure when last to leave.
